title: A/B experimental design with power analysis for honest sycophancy benchmarking

original_idea.body:
# A/B experimental design with power analysis for honest sycophancy benchmarking

**Problem:** Sycophancy results (e.g., 10% course-correction under pressure) are reported without experimental rigor — no power analysis, no control of confounds — so it's unclear which differences across models are real versus noise.

**Direction:** Import randomized controlled experiment design and power analysis from clinical/social-science statistics. Construct a sycophancy stress test as a proper factorial experiment (pressure type x topic x model), pre-register effect sizes, compute required sample sizes via power analysis, randomize prompt order, and report confidence intervals and effect sizes for the prompted-vs-unprompted sycophancy gap across open models.

**Why it matters:** Replaces eyeballed sycophancy numbers with statistically defensible estimates and reusable methodology — addressing the realistic-sycophancy-evaluation gap. No training; pure experimental rigor applied to behavioral probing.

**Relevant context:** Grounded in Claude Opus 4.5 system card sycophancy finding and landscape honesty_faithfulness gap on realistic sycophancy evaluation. Source subfield: experimental design / biostatistics. Target subfield: honesty_faithfulness.
